chunks: Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about prayer on a ship. He said: 'He should face the Qiblah. When it turns, if he is able to face the Qiblah, let him do so; otherwise, let him pray wherever it carries him.' He said: 'If he is able to stand, let him pray standing; otherwise, let him sit and then pray.'
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim perform prayer on a moving ship according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *taysir* (ease) in ritual prayer during maritime travel, prioritizing the stability of the Qiblah direction over rigid postural requirements. It reflects the Shia juristic view that physical constraints, such as a ship's rolling, permit adjusting both orientation and posture (standing to sitting) to maintain the integrity of the prayer without undue hardship.
